sentences.text: How fast is this curve rising, {here}right here?
sentences.spoken: How fast is this curve rising, right here?

sentences.text: The curve is {name}y equals x squared, and its steepness {changes}changes from point to point.
sentences.spoken: The curve is y equals x squared, and its steepness changes from point to point.

sentences.text: Pick two points on the curve: {p1}x equals one, and {p2}x equals two.
sentences.spoken: Pick two points on the curve: x equals one, and x equals two.

sentences.text: The line through them is a secant. It rises {rise}three over a run of one, so its slope is {three}three.
sentences.spoken: The line through them is a secant. It rises three over a run of one, so its slope is three.

sentences.text: Now slide the second point toward the first. The gap h shrinks: {half}a half, {tenth}a tenth.
sentences.spoken: Now slide the second point toward the first. The gap h shrinks: a half, a tenth.

sentences.text: The secant pivots {tangent}into the tangent line, and its slope settles on {two}exactly two.
sentences.spoken: The secant pivots into the tangent line, and its slope settles on exactly two.

sentences.text: Do the same at every point. At {x2}two, the slope is four. At {x3}three, it is six.
sentences.spoken: Do the same at every point. At two, the slope is four. At three, it is six.
The slope is always twice x.

sentences.text: The algebra agrees. {expand}Expand the quotient, {cancel}cancel the h, and let h go to {zero}zero: the derivative of x squared is {lands}two x.
sentences.spoken: The algebra agrees. Expand the quotient, cancel the h, and let h go to zero: the derivative of x squared is two x.

sentences.text: For x cubed, the same steps give {cube}three x squared.
sentences.spoken: For x cubed, the same steps give three x squared.

sentences.text: So for any power: {rule}bring the power down, then lower it by one.
sentences.spoken: So for any power: bring the power down, then lower it by one.

sentences.text: The derivative is the slope of the tangent: {limit}the limit of secant slopes, {rule}with one rule for every power.
sentences.spoken: The derivative is the slope of the tangent: the limit of secant slopes, with one rule for every power.
